_readme: The application-specific half of the drill. The harness (load-drill.sh, k6 scripts)
knows nothing about Waa; everything app-shaped lives here, so pointing the drill at a
different .NET service is editing this file and nothing else.
'fixtures' are SQL queries run against the restored database before the drill starts.
Each one fills a named list the scenarios draw from at random. This is what stops the
test from hammering a single row: real traffic spreads across slugs, and a benchmark
that reads one row measures the buffer cache, not the database.
'weight' is relative pick frequency within a scenario, not a percentage.

slugs.query: SELECT "PublicSlug" FROM "EventInfos" WHERE "PublicSlug" IS NOT NULL ORDER BY random() LIMIT 200
slugs.onEmpty: The public-event read is the hot path of this app; with no published events the drill would measure 404s. Restore a dump that has some, or drop the read from 'traffic' below.

traffic.name: public-event-snapshot
traffic.note: The hot path — every invite open hits it. Rate-limited by the 'public' policy (64/min per IP), which is why the harness varies the client IP per VU.

traffic.name: client-config
traffic.note: Fetched on every SPA load, so it rides along with every real visit.

health.note: Exempt from rate limiting by design, so the harness can probe them freely during a drill.

note: ClientIpMiddleware trusts CF-Connecting-IP and X-Forwarded-For from loopback and RFC1918
sources. A drill runs from exactly such a source, so each VU can present its own client IP.
Without this the whole load collapses into one rate-limit partition and the drill measures
the rate limiter (64 req/min) instead of the connection pool — roughly 1 req/s, which would
look like a pass while proving nothing.

pools._readme: Per-connection-string Maximum Pool Size, mirroring the app's ConnectionStrings. The drill uses these to tell 'the pool is the ceiling' apart from 'Postgres is the ceiling' — the two failures look identical from the outside and have opposite fixes.

deployment._readme: Blue/green doubles the connection budget for the length of a drain — the window this whole drill exists to size. Used by the verdict to compute worst-case headroom.
deployment.note: instances = how many applications share this Postgres (api.waa.ro + api.waa.events).
